title: The whipping lousy Lucy gave him
html_source:
Sir Thomas Lucy (1532-1600), a gentleman and owner of lands in Warwickshire. Some sources report that Shakespeare was whipped or imprisoned by Lucy for poaching on Lucy’s land, which was one cause of Shakespeare’s move to London.

There is a ballad attributed to Shakespeare which lampoons Lucy, punning his name with “lousy”:

A parliament member, a justice of peace,
At home a poor scarecrow, at London an ass,
If lousy is Lucy as some folks miscall it
Then Lucy is lousy whatever befall it.

This ballad suggests that Lucy’s wife was unfaithful to him, keeping with Stephen’s theme about Shakespeare.
